newsitem.title: USA: Dlr closes higher with bond, stock updraft in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Dlr closes higher with bond, stock updraft in U.S.

text.p: *Dlr/yen falters above 110.50, after edging past post-GDP high.
*Resistance from mark/yen; seen unable to surpass 73 near-term.
*Dollar breaks above 1.2425 against the Swissy. Analysts see reported fund buying technically motivated.
*Dlr/mark, yen supported gains by in stocks and bonds
*Dlr/mark well supported by reported orders at 1.5085.
The dollar closed higher along with U.S. bonds and stocks which surged on surprisingly low U.S. inflation and retail sales data.
But after the data, the dollar struggled to exceed fresh eight-week highs set earlier against the mark and yen.
Traders expressed concern that the fall in U.S. interest rates, which move in the opposite direction from bond prices, might undermine demand for dollars.
"The underpinning is provided by the bond and stock market," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer and Co.
"It's keeping the dollar from collapsing, because clearly those numbers were bearish, as far as interest rates are concered."
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds soared almost one-and-a-half points after the government said consumer prices rose a slight 0.1 percent and retail sales advanced a tepid 0.2 percent in August.
The dollar closed at 1.5135/45 marks, up from 1.5122/27 at the open and at 110.46/49 yen up from 110.37/40.
Wall street economists expected retail prices to rise two-tenths of a percent and sales to rise seven-tenths.

The dollar has posted new highs each day for a week, amid speculation that the Federal Reserve would raise short-term interest rates slightly to keep too rapid a pace of economic expansion from generating faster inflation.
"The Fed may not move," said Strauss. "That is going to be good for bonds and stocks but clearly puts a damper here on dollar."

The Dow Jones Industrial stock average rose almost 67 points to a new record high on Friday, in response to hopes the Fed may not act to slow the economy when its policy-making body meets on September 24.
Technical buying of dollars against the Swiss franc and yen led the way higher, traders said.
The dollar closed at 1.2434/41 Swiss -- its highest level since July 16 -- up from 1.2375/85 at the open.
The dollar rose to 110.52 against the yen, its highest since July 15. This slightly surpassed the high set early Friday after Japan's economy fell 0.7 percent in the April through June quarter.

"There has been good demand for dollar/yen," said Dennis Pettit, foreign exchange manager at Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan. "But equally there must be some commercial selling interest on the way up, because we're not breaking away as quickly as one might have imagined."
Japan's struggles to emerge from a prolonged recession have all but eliminated chances of interest rates in Japan rising from near record lows this year.
"Japan's economy is still muddling along," said David Gilmore, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics. "So that is going to be bearish for yen for the next month or so."
In other trade, the dollar closed at Canadian $1.3696/01, down from C$1.3720/25.
The pound closed at $1.5551/59, up from $1.5545/55.
The Australian dollar fell to $0.7905/10 from $0.7959/64.
-- Alden Bentley 212-859-1667
